cards.title: The War Room — Inception
cards.description:
Whiteboards wall-to-wall, sticky notes, napkin sketches. A monitor reads: "BOLT #001 — STARTED. Time remaining: 15:00."

The PO gave the Agent one line — "customer feedback portal" — and it came back with a full spec: three user stories, each with who/what/why. Some of those options it invented.
cards.image_prompt: Modern startup war room with whiteboards covered in sticky notes, large wall monitor showing a project plan and countdown timer, glass walls, ergonomic chairs, warm lighting, mid-century modern aesthetic, isometric digital illustration

cards.title: The PO 📋
cards.description: The Product Owner. Smart, busy, vague. Cares about outcomes — not technology. Will absolutely give you a one-line spec and expect a working product by end of Bolt.
cards.image_prompt: Confident product owner in a smart-casual blazer holding a coffee cup and a sticky note, mid-explanation, modern office background, single character portrait

cards.title: Spec Board
cards.description:
The Agent's draft spec: three user stories from the PO's one line. For each, it lists options for WHO uses it, WHAT they do, WHY it matters. Some are right. Others are invention — crypto rewards, surveillance, social auto-posting.

Pick the option matching the PO's real intent, every who/what/why, every story.
cards.image_prompt: Digital whiteboard displaying three user-story panels, each with a who/what/why row of options, some options glowing faintly red as if uncertain, modern UI, soft blue ambient light, single object on dark background

cards.title: Spec Validated. Two tracks open.
cards.description:
Every who/what/why locks in green. Customer submits feedback. Customer sees confirmation. Admin reads the list. The hallucinated options — crypto, surveillance, auto-post — grey out and slide off the board.

The Agent, from the corner: "Spec locked. Now I need two things in parallel — curate my context, and verify my architecture. Split up. Meet me in the Review Room when both are done."

Two doors open. Context Lab. Architecture Bay.

cards.title: The Context Lab — Context Management
cards.description:
A glass wall shows the Agent's working memory: a stack of docs for the Feedback Portal. Too tall. The capacity gauge reads OVER BUDGET, and the build stream stutters — "wiring MongoDB next to DynamoDB… adding crypto rewards…"

A note from the Agent: "I loaded everything I could find. Most of it is stale. Help me trim it."
cards.image_prompt: Modern architecture design studio with a large glass wall displaying a stack of document icons next to a capacity gauge and a live scrolling build log, some documents marked with red warning halos, sketches on the floor, holographic UI, blue and orange accent lighting, isometric digital illustration

discoveries.label: Read the 'Context is King' card pinned to the wall

cards.title: Agent Memory Panel
cards.description:
The Agent's working memory, exposed. The build stream is producing contradictions because half the docs in its head are stale or off-spec.

• Current (requirements, architecture, API contract) — keep loaded.
• Stale (Marcus's MongoDB design, v1 draft with cut features) — poisoning the output.
• Off-spec (brainstorm with crypto/AR, social auto-post spec) — features the PO killed.

Remove docs until the build stream goes green and the gauge fits the budget.
cards.image_prompt: Tech context panel on a glass surface showing a vertical list of document cards next to a vertical capacity bar, with a scrolling stream of build log lines below, some entries red and some green, modern UI, single object on dark background

cards.title: Context Curated.
cards.description:
Stale docs vanish from the panel. The capacity gauge drops back into the green. The build stream stabilizes — every line now reads ✅ on a real component of the actual spec.

A sealed Context Package prints from a slot in the wall.

cards.title: Lore Card — "Context is King"
cards.description:
Most AI failures aren't IQ failures — they're context failures.

Load the right docs (current specs, current code) and the agent is brilliant. Feed it stale or missing context and it confidently builds the wrong thing. Feed it too much context and the relevant docs get crowded out by the irrelevant ones.

A good prompt + the right context > a clever prompt + everything-and-the-kitchen-sink.
cards.image_prompt: Stylized infographic card with a stack of documents flowing into a robot's open chest panel, blue and gold gradient, 'CONTEXT' label, single object on dark background

cards.title: Context Package
cards.description:
A sealed manifest listing exactly the docs the Agent should have in memory for this Bolt: current requirements, current architecture, locked API contract. Everything else stripped out.

Bring this to the Review Room. The mob-construction step needs it loaded before the Agent starts executing.
cards.image_prompt: A sealed manifest card labeled 'CONTEXT PACKAGE' with three neatly stacked document icons and a green checkmark seal, soft blue glow, single object on dark background

cards.title: The Architecture Bay — Construction Design
cards.description:
The Agent has drafted a layered architecture — presentation, application, data, infrastructure. Eight AWS components queue for placement.

On the side bench, two loose blueprints: Lambda and CloudFront, with a warning taped on. "DO NOT WIRE THESE DIRECTLY. There's an API layer between them for a reason."
cards.image_prompt: Modern developer workshop with a large vertical architecture diagram showing four labeled layers stacked top-to-bottom, a queue of unplaced AWS component cards waiting on the side, two loose blueprint cards flagged with red warning tape on a side bench, warm overhead lights, isometric digital illustration

discoveries.label: Read the 'Anti-Patterns' card on the wall
Pick up the loose Lambda blueprint
Pick up the loose CloudFront blueprint

cards.title: Architecture Diagram
cards.description:
Four layers: Presentation, Application, Data, Infrastructure. Eight components queue one at a time — React, CloudFront, API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, CDK Stack, IAM Roles.

Decide the layer for each. Misplace one and the diagram explains why it doesn't fit.
cards.image_prompt: A vertical cross-section of a building with four labeled floors — Presentation, Application, Data, Infrastructure — each containing AWS service icons, blueprint aesthetic, single object on dark background

cards.title: Architecture Verified.
cards.description:
Every component locks onto its correct floor. React and CloudFront glow at the top. API Gateway and Lambda settle in the middle. DynamoDB and S3 anchor the data layer. CDK and IAM hold the foundation.

A sealed Architecture Package prints from a slot in the wall.

cards.title: Lore Card — "Anti-Patterns"
cards.description:
Common AI-DLC anti-patterns:

• Single-shotting a multi-step problem — let the agent break it down.
• Skipping the verify step — "it looked right" ≠ "it is right."
• Stale or oversized context — the agent will gladly build last week's design today.
• Wiring across layers — Lambda direct to CloudFront, frontend direct to DB. Layers exist for a reason.

The loop exists because every one of these has shipped to prod somewhere.
cards.image_prompt: Stylized infographic card with four warning icons arranged as a 2x2 grid, each labeled with a different AI anti-pattern, red and amber accents, single object on dark background

cards.title: Architecture Package
cards.description:
A sealed blueprint listing the verified four-layer architecture: React + CloudFront up top, API Gateway + Lambda in the middle, DynamoDB + S3 in data, CDK + IAM at the foundation. Boundaries clean, dependencies one-way.

Bring this to the Review Room. The mob-construction step needs the layers locked in before the Agent starts building.
cards.image_prompt: A sealed blueprint card labeled 'ARCHITECTURE PACKAGE' with four horizontal layered bars in different colors and a green checkmark seal, soft blue glow, single object on dark background

cards.title: Loose Blueprint: Lambda
cards.description: A standalone blueprint card for an AWS Lambda function. Handles business logic. Not meant to talk to the frontend directly — it lives behind an API Gateway.
cards.image_prompt: Blueprint card labeled 'LAMBDA' with a lambda function symbol and warning tape across one corner, single object on dark background

cards.title: Loose Blueprint: CloudFront
cards.description: A standalone blueprint card for CloudFront CDN. Serves the frontend at the edge. Not meant to talk to Lambda directly — traffic goes through the API layer first.
cards.image_prompt: Blueprint card labeled 'CLOUDFRONT' with a globe icon and warning tape across one corner, single object on dark background

cards.title: Anti-Pattern Triggered!
cards.description: You wired Lambda directly to CloudFront with no API layer. The internet screams. Somewhere, a security engineer wakes up in a cold sweat. -10 seconds.

cards.title: Both Packages Ready.
cards.description:
You lock the Context Package and the Architecture Package into the transfer console. The far wall dims, then reveals a doorway lit from within.

The Agent, over the intercom: "Both packages received. I'm loading them now. Come to the Review Room — I'm about to execute end-to-end, and I want you watching every step."

cards.title: The Review Room — Mob Construction
cards.description:
One long console. Six coffee cups along the top, one per subsystem the Agent is about to bring online: Spec, Context, Arch, Code, Deploy, Verify.

The Agent: "I've got your context and your architecture. I'll execute the whole loop in front of you, pausing at each step for you to confirm the outcome. Watch for what looks right but isn't."
cards.image_prompt: Long console down the center of a quiet review room, six illuminated cup-sized indicator slots along the top of the console, an AI agent character at the console mid-gesture, holographic build progress on the far wall, cool blue-and-amber lighting, isometric digital illustration

discoveries.label: Read the 'The Loop' card on the wall

cards.title: The Agent 🤖 (Review Room)
cards.description: Your AI partner. Different from the drafts you saw earlier — this one is loaded with the exact context you curated and the exact architecture you verified. It's about to execute the whole build in front of you.
cards.image_prompt: Friendly humanoid AI assistant standing at a long console with six cup-shaped indicator slots, holographic build stream visible in the background, soft glowing blue chassis, single character portrait

cards.title: Live Build Console
cards.description:
Six steps queued: Spec → Context → Arch → Code → Deploy → Verify. At each one the Agent proposes an action and offers three options. Pick the one matching the outcome you actually want.

One wrong approval breaks the chain and costs you seconds.
cards.image_prompt: Long digital console showing six numbered execution steps arranged as coffee-cup indicators, each with three option buttons below, a build stream scrolling in the background, single object on dark background

cards.title: Outcome Verified.
cards.description:
The sixth cup lights green. Every step of the Agent's execution has been confirmed, live, against the spec you validated and the architecture you designed. No hallucinations slipped through. No poisoned context. No skipped verify.

The Agent: "That's Mob Construction done. The build is real. Deploy pipeline is armed. Launch Pad's open. Last stop."

cards.title: Lore Card — "The Loop"
cards.description:
AI-DLC core loop:

1. Inception — human intent, AI proposes spec, human verifies.
2. Context Management — human curates working memory.
3. Construction Design — AI proposes architecture, human verifies.
4. Mob Construction — AI executes, humans verify each outcome.
5. Operations — deploy, monitor, iterate.

AI proposes. Humans decide. At every step. Skip a verify and you ship the wrong thing — fast.
cards.image_prompt: Stylized infographic card showing a five-step circular loop labeled AI-DLC, alternating human and robot icons, blue and orange gradient, single object on dark background

cards.title: The Launch Pad — Operations
cards.description:
Mission control. The deploy is already in flight — CDK stack pushed, frontend uploaded — but two indicators flash red. CORS errors. Missing env var. A timer reads "DEFUSE: 0:45" and ticks down.

Switches, one input, a countdown. The 'skip tests' toggle is the trap.
cards.image_prompt: Mission control style room with a wall of monitors showing a live deploy console with two red error indicators, a large defuse-style countdown timer reading 0:45, stage banner visible reading 'STAGE: prod', dramatic cool lighting, isometric digital illustration

cards.title: Deploy Console (Live)
cards.description:
The deploy is in flight and broken. Forty-five seconds.

• Add CORS headers to Lambda response — needed (browser preflight failing)
• Redeploy API Gateway stage — needed (so the headers take effect)
• Skip integration tests — TRAP (never skip verify under pressure)
• API Gateway stage name — the standard prod stage value
cards.image_prompt: Digital deploy console with toggle switches and a single text input, two red error indicators above, a countdown timer in the corner, single object on dark background

cards.title: Shipped! The Bolt is complete.
cards.description:
CORS headers go on. The API redeploys. Tests run — you didn't skip them, and they pass. Stage name locks in as "prod." The defuse timer freezes with seconds to spare and flips to ✅ DEFUSED.

The Feedback Portal goes live. The PO refreshes their browser. Customer feedback starts flowing in.

The Agent: "We did the loop. I proposed — you verified. I refined — you approved. I executed — you confirmed the outcome. That's AI-DLC."

The PO: "That's exactly what I asked for. Not an approximation. Not a hallucination. What I actually asked for."

The Bolt closes. Same time tomorrow.
